question: Which of the following practices should nurses emphasize when educating communities about preventing foodborne infections?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of food preservation including canning and salting
options.B: Refrigerating all fresh vegetables without ever washing them with water
options.C: Practicing rigorous hand hygiene and ensuring safe food storage temperatures
options.D: Consuming raw dairy products to maximize beneficial live bacterial intake

explanation: Basic hygiene and temperature control are the most effective measures individuals and families can take to prevent microbial contamination and foodborne illness at home. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of the scientific discipline known as entomology?

options.A: The investigation of bacterial pathogens
options.B: The analysis of soil mineral composition
options.C: The examination of parasitic protozoa
options.D: The scientific study of insects

explanation: Entomology is specifically dedicated to examining the biology, behavior, and ecology of insects. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h1)

question: To which biological phylum do insects belong?

options.A: Chordata
options.B: Mollusca
options.C: Arthropoda
options.D: Annelida

explanation: Insects are classified under the phylum Arthropoda, sharing jointed limbs and exoskeletons with spiders and crustaceans. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h1)

question: What are the three main body segments of an adult insect?

options.A: Head, thorax, and abdomen
options.B: Cephalothorax, thorax, and tail
options.C: Head, abdomen, and wings
options.D: Thorax, pelvis, and abdomen

explanation: The insect body plan is strictly tripartite, consisting of the head, thorax, and abdomen. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h2)

question: How do insects primarily exchange respiratory gases with their environment?

options.A: By means of thin, vascularized skin diffusion across the abdomen
options.B: Through active pumping mechanisms inside the segmented head
options.C: Using specialized lung-like book gills located near the thorax
options.D: Through internal tracheal tubes connected to lateral spiracles

explanation: Insects lack lungs and instead rely on an extensive network of trachea that deliver oxygen directly to tissues via external openings called spiracles. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h2)

question: Which insect order contains mosquitoes and houseflies?

options.A: Diptera
options.B: Coleoptera
options.C: Siphonaptera
options.D: Hemiptera

explanation: Diptera translates to two wings, identifying true flies and mosquitoes which are primary vectors of human pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following insect orders consists entirely of wingless ectoparasites that jump and transmit plague?

options.A: Orthoptera
options.B: Siphonaptera
options.C: Hymenoptera
options.D: Lepidoptera

explanation: Fleas belong to Siphonaptera and are flattened parasites known historically for vectoring Yersinia pestis. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h3)

question: What are the four stages of complete metamorphosis in the correct chronological order?

options.A: Egg, nymph, pupa, adult
options.B: Larva, egg, adult, pupa
options.C: Nymph, larva, adult, egg
options.D: Egg, larva, pupa, adult

explanation: Holometabolous insects transition through an egg, a feeding larva, a non-feeding transformative pupa, and a flying or mobile adult. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h4)

question: How do nymphs differ fundamentally from larvae in insect development?

options.A: Larvae undergo a resting pupal stage, while nymphs do not pass through a pupal phase
options.B: Nymphs resemble small, wingless adults, whereas larvae look completely different from adults
options.C: Larvae possess compound eyes and jointed legs, whereas nymphs lack any visible limbs
options.D: Nymphs are strictly aquatic, while all insect larvae live exclusively in terrestrial soil

explanation: Hemimetabolous nymphs share body plans and ecological niches with adults, unlike worm-like holometabolous larvae. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h4)

question: What distinguishes biological transmission of a pathogen from mechanical transmission?

options.A: The pathogen multiplies or develops inside the vector's body tissues
options.B: Infection occurs rapidly through direct contact with an uninfected insect cuticle
options.C: The disease agent is transmitted without any physical contact with human skin
options.D: The insect carries the pathogen exclusively on its external feet and wings

explanation: Biological vectors serve as essential hosts where parasites complete parts of their life cycle before transmission. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a method by which insects directly cause clinical harm to humans?

options.A: Envenomation through painful stings
options.B: Biological vectoring of malaria parasites
options.C: Mechanical transmission of enteric bacteria
options.D: Photosynthetic toxin release

explanation: Insects are heterotrophic animals and do not engage in photosynthesis or produce photosynthetic toxins. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which vector is primarily responsible for transmitting the parasite that causes malaria in Nigeria?

options.A: Aedes aegypti mosquito
options.B: Phlebotomus sandfly
options.C: Simulium blackfly
options.D: Female Anopheles mosquito

explanation: Female Anopheles mosquitoes are the definitive biological vectors for human malaria parasites. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h6)

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian riverine area encounters several patients presenting with severe skin lesions and ocular damage leading to river blindness. Which insect vector is most likely implicated?

options.A: Bed bug
options.B: Simulium blackfly
options.C: Tsetse fly
options.D: Housefly

explanation: Simulium blackflies breed in fast-flowing rivers and transmit Onchocerca volvulus, the causative agent of river blindness. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary objective of Integrated Vector Management (IVM) in public health?

options.A: Eliminating natural predators to encourage rapid population growth of beneficial insects
options.B: Relying solely on high-dose chemical pesticides to eradicate all insects in an ecosystem
options.C: Combining multiple environmental, chemical, and biological strategies for sustainable vector control
options.D: Treating infected human patients exclusively without addressing external insect vectors

explanation: IVM promotes a balanced, multi-pronged approach to prevent resistance and reduce environmental impact while controlling vector populations. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h7)

question: Which activity represents an environmental management method for mosquito control?

options.A: Draining stagnant water puddles near residential housing
options.B: Spraying synthetic pyrethroid insecticides inside bedrooms
options.C: Introducing antibiotic therapies to treat clinical bacterial infections
options.D: Distributing anti-malarial pharmaceutical drugs to pregnant women

explanation: Environmental management targets vector breeding habitats by removing stagnant water sources where mosquitoes lay eggs. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h7)

question: What proportion of total health care waste is generally classified as non-hazardous general waste?

options.A: Exactly fifty percent
options.B: Seventy-five to ninety percent
options.C: Ten to twenty-five percent
options.D: Ninety-five to ninety-nine percent

explanation: The vast majority of materials produced in healthcare facilities are harmless general refuse comparable to household garbage. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h1)

question: Why is proper categorization at the point of generation considered the foundation of safe health care waste management?

options.A: It ensures all waste can be recycled into commercial products
options.B: It eliminates the need for any subsequent incineration
options.C: It reduces total municipal garbage collection fees
options.D: It prevents hazardous materials from contaminating safe waste streams

explanation: Separating hazardous from non-hazardous items immediately prevents safe waste from becoming dangerous and costly to treat. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h1)

question: Which of the following items belongs to the general health care waste stream?

options.A: Cardboard boxes from supplies
options.B: Blood-soaked gauze dressings
options.C: Used surgical scalpel blades
options.D: Expired chemotherapy drugs

explanation: Administrative and packaging supplies are non-hazardous and belong with general municipal waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h2)

question: What is the primary operational benefit of keeping general waste separate from clinical waste in a hospital?

options.A: It prevents needle-stick injuries among administrative staff
options.B: It allows all hospital waste to be safely composted on-site
options.C: It avoids overloading expensive clinical waste treatment systems
options.D: It eliminates the requirement for municipal waste trucks

explanation: Treating harmless paper and food waste through medical incinerators wastes scarce resources and capacity. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h2)

question: Human tissues, organs, and recognizable body parts generated during surgery are classified as what type of waste?

options.A: Pharmaceutical waste
options.B: Radioactive waste
options.C: General domestic waste
options.D: Pathological waste

explanation: Anatomical parts, tissues, and organs fall specifically under the pathological waste classification. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h3)

question: A patient's dressing soaked with purulent wound exudate should be disposed of as:

options.A: General office refuse
options.B: Infectious waste
options.C: Recyclable plastic
options.D: Chemical waste

explanation: Items contaminated with blood or body fluids contain potential pathogens and require infectious waste management. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary reason healthcare personnel must avoid recapping needles after injection?

options.A: It causes the syringe barrel to crack
options.B: It dulls the sharp tip for subsequent patients
options.C: It increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It violates standard drug reconstitution guidelines

explanation: Attempting to guide a needle back into its cap frequently results in accidental puncture of the hand holding the cap. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h4)

question: A nurse finishes drawing blood with a winged infusion set. Where should the needle be placed immediately?

options.A: Inside a rigid, puncture-resistant sharps container
options.B: Inside a soft red polythene garbage bag
options.C: On a clean tray for later dismantling
options.D: In the black bag designated for general refuse

explanation: All sharps must go straight into a puncture-proof container at the point of use to protect staff and handlers. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h4)

question: Expired antibiotics and unused vaccines found in a clinic dispensary are classified as:

options.A: Pathological waste
options.B: Infectious waste
options.C: Radioactive waste
options.D: Pharmaceutical waste

explanation: Unused, outdated, or contaminated medicinal drugs and vaccines fall under pharmaceutical waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h5)

question: Why do cytotoxic drugs require specialized handling distinct from standard pharmaceutical waste?

options.A: They can spontaneously explode when exposed to air
options.B: They attract insects and rodents if left in open bins
options.C: They possess cell-damaging, carcinogenic, and mutagenic properties
options.D: They are extremely expensive and require inventory tracking

explanation: Cytotoxic agents are designed to kill cells and pose serious health risks to handlers if environmental exposure occurs. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h5)

question: Discarded liquid disinfectants and mercury from broken clinical thermometers are examples of what waste type?

options.A: Infectious waste
options.B: Chemical waste
options.C: General waste
options.D: Pathological waste

explanation: Solvents, disinfectants, and heavy metals like mercury are categorized as chemical waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h6)

question: Which material is a characteristic source of radioactive waste within a modern medical facility?

options.A: Cardboard shipping cartons
options.B: Expired paracetamol tablets
options.C: Isotopes used in cancer radiotherapy
options.D: Used cotton wool balls

explanation: Radiotherapy and nuclear medicine departments generate radioactive waste from diagnostic and therapeutic radioisotopes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of color-coding waste receptacles in clinical settings?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing waste bags
options.B: To comply with international interior design codes
options.C: To allow instant visual identification of waste categories and prevent sorting errors
options.D: To make hospital wards look clean and aesthetically pleasing

explanation: Color coding provides a universal visual cue so staff can deposit items into the correct container instantly. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h7)

question: According to standard waste management guidelines, which color container is typically designated for infectious clinical waste?

options.A: Black
options.B: Clear
options.C: White
options.D: Yellow

explanation: Yellow bins bearing the biohazard symbol are universally utilized for infectious waste items. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h7)

question: What primary characteristic distinguishes health care waste from ordinary municipal refuse?

options.A: It is generated strictly within surgical and intensive care environments
options.B: It requires immediate chemical stabilization before leaving the bedside
options.C: It is exclusively composed of non-biodegradable plastics and metals
options.D: It contains a high concentration of pathogenic microorganisms and hazardous substances

explanation: Medical waste carries biological agents and toxic materials that pose direct health threats, separating it from standard household garbage. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: Why do discarded items like used cotton gauze and blood tubing present significant microbiological dangers?

options.A: They immediately attract vector insects that carry airborne fungal spores
options.B: They release toxic chemical gases upon drying out
options.C: They provide organic moisture and nutrients that support rapid bacterial growth
options.D: They neutralize standard hospital disinfectants

explanation: Body fluids and organic tissue remnants trapped in porous materials create a fertile breeding ground for infectious agents. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h1)

question: Which color receptacle is universally designated for collecting used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades?

options.A: Black non-perforated bucket
options.B: Brown heavy-duty chemical bin
options.C: Translucent white plastic bag
options.D: Yellow puncture-resistant safety box

explanation: Sharps require rigid, puncture-proof containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries during handling and transport. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary operational purpose of color-coding waste receptacles in a clinical setting?

options.A: To simplify aesthetic organization within busy hospital wards
options.B: To prevent the dangerous mixing of hazardous materials with general refuse
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing specialized disposal bags
options.D: To comply with international branding standards for pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Color-coding allows immediate visual identification, ensuring that infectious or toxic items do not end up in municipal landfills. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: A healthcare worker sustains a puncture injury from a discarded needle left loosely on a medication tray. Which bloodborne pathogens represent the primary transmission risks in this scenario?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and influenza virus
options.B: Cholera vibrio and Shigella dysenteriae
options.C: Malaria parasites and typhoid bacilli
options.D: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Sharps injuries directly inoculate contaminated blood into the vascular system, making bloodborne viral pathogens the chief occupational concern. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common route of pathogen transmission resulting from poorly managed hospital waste?

options.A: Ingestion of contaminated groundwater near open dump sites
options.B: Contact with contaminated items by informal waste pickers
options.C: Direct inhalation of intact viral particles through unbroken skin
options.D: Percutaneous injury from stray needles

explanation: Skin serves as a protective barrier against intact viruses; pathogens typically enter the body through breaks in the skin, mucous membranes, ingestion, or inhalation of aerosols, not directly through healthy skin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h3)

question: What environmental hazard is created by the open-air burning of medical plastics and PVC packaging?

options.A: Immediate soil alkalization that prevents plant growth
options.B: Depletion of the local groundwater table
options.C: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the atmosphere
options.D: Generation of radioactive particulate fallout

explanation: Low-temperature or open burning of chlorinated plastics creates dangerous chemical pollutants that persist in the environment and harm human health. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: Which animal vectors are most commonly attracted to improperly stored organic medical waste in community dumpsites?

options.A: Grazing cattle and sheep
options.B: Aquatic snails and freshwater fish
options.C: Pollinating bees and butterflies
options.D: Rats, flies, and stray dogs

explanation: Organic medical waste provides an abundant food source for scavengers and vermin, which then act as vectors spreading disease into nearby communities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: At what capacity should a sharps box or infectious waste bag be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: Whenever an inspector visits the ward
options.B: Only at the end of each calendar week
options.C: When it reaches the three-quarters full mark
options.D: When completely full to maximize storage space

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters capacity prevents overflow, accidental punctures, and spillage during handling and closure. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: Why is post-disposal sorting or rummaging through mixed hospital waste strictly prohibited?

options.A: It causes chemical reactions that generate noxious odors
options.B: It drastically increases the incidence of accidental needle-stick injuries and pathogen exposure
options.C: It violates hospital administrative budgeting rules
options.D: It slows down the discharge process for recovering patients

explanation: Attempting to sort mixed waste forces handlers to blindly rifle through dangerous materials, directly exposing them to hidden sharps and infectious matter. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which an autoclave neutralizes infectious waste?

options.A: High-pressure saturated steam achieving sterilization temperatures
options.B: Chemical oxidation using concentrated chlorine bleach
options.C: Thermal melting via direct open-flame exposure
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation destroying cellular DNA

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to destroy all microbial life on contaminated instruments and medical waste materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: What purpose does encapsulation serve when managing hazardous medical items like used sharps in resource-constrained facilities?

options.A: It immobilizes and seals waste inside solid blocks of mortar or plastic to prevent access
options.B: It bleaches fabrics to allow safe laundering and reuse
options.C: It converts biohazardous material into organic fertilizer for farming
options.D: It evaporates liquid chemicals into harmless ambient gases

explanation: Encapsulation traps sharps and residues within a solid matrix, preventing scavenging and accidental injuries before final burial. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h6)

question: What is a core clinical responsibility of ward nurses regarding health care waste?

options.A: Operating industrial-grade hospital incinerators
options.B: Designing municipal sewage treatment plants
options.C: Purchasing waste receptacles from commercial vendors
options.D: Modeling correct segregation and supervising junior personnel

explanation: Nurses set the standard for safe daily practice on the ward and oversee proper compliance by support staff and students. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)

question: A staff nurse notices a junior colleague casually tossing a used syringe into a regular black household waste bin. What is the most appropriate immediate action for the nurse to take?

options.A: Ignore the incident to avoid creating interpersonal tension on the busy ward
options.B: Quietly retrieve the syringe later without mentioning it to anyone
options.C: Report the junior colleague directly to the hospital board for immediate termination
options.D: Correct the action immediately, explaining the biohazard risk and proper bin usage

explanation: Immediate, constructive correction reinforces safety culture and prevents hazardous items from entering municipal waste streams. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)

question: What percentage of total waste generated in healthcare facilities typically consists of general non-hazardous waste?

options.A: Seventy-five to ninety percent
options.B: Forty to fifty percent
options.C: Ninety-five to one hundred percent
options.D: Ten to twenty-five percent

explanation: The vast majority of waste produced in a healthcare setting is routine, non-hazardous refuse similar to household garbage. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: Why is the proper classification of healthcare waste considered a foundational step for safe hospital operations?

options.A: It eliminates the need for personal protective equipment among waste handlers
options.B: It dictates the appropriate treatment and disposal methods required to neutralize specific hazards
options.C: It ensures that all hospital waste can be recycled into commercial products
options.D: It reduces the overall volume of waste generated by clinical departments

explanation: Different categories of waste carry unique risks and require specific handling, treatment, and disposal pathways to prevent harm. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: Which category of healthcare waste includes discarded needles, scalpels, and broken glass ampoules?

options.A: Pathological waste
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Sharps waste
options.D: Genotoxic waste

explanation: Sharps encompass any instrument or object capable of puncturing or cutting the skin, posing an immediate physical and infectious risk. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: A nurse discards empty vials of chemotherapy medications used for oncology patients. Into which specialized waste category do these items fall?

options.A: General domestic refuse
options.B: Pathological tissue waste
options.C: Infectious biological waste
options.D: Genotoxic and chemical waste

explanation: Cytotoxic drugs and their contaminated containers are classified as genotoxic or hazardous chemical waste due to their cell-damaging properties. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of waste minimization strategies in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Lowering the requirement for staff hand hygiene practices
options.B: Eliminating the need for colored waste receptacles
options.C: Reducing the total volume and hazard level of waste produced
options.D: Increasing the speed of waste collection across clinical wards

explanation: Waste minimization focuses on source reduction to lessen the environmental footprint and management costs of refuse. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: How does careful procurement practice contribute directly to effective health care waste management?

options.A: By ensuring all clinical departments use the exact same brand of disposable syringes
options.B: By purchasing cheaper equipment that can be discarded immediately after a single use
options.C: By selecting supplies with reduced packaging and longer shelf lives to prevent unnecessary disposal
options.D: By outsourcing waste transport contracts to private international companies

explanation: Smart purchasing prevents the accumulation of excess or single-use items that ultimately add to the facility's waste burden. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: At what exact location must healthcare waste segregation take place?

options.A: During the final sorting at the landfill
options.B: Inside the temporary storage holding room
options.C: At the central municipal incinerator site
options.D: At the point of origin where the waste is generated

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately by the person generating the waste to prevent mixing hazardous and non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h4)

question: What occurs when general paper waste is incorrectly discarded into a yellow biohazard container?

options.A: The biological hazard level of the infectious waste is effectively neutralized
options.B: The physical safety of sharps collection boxes is significantly improved
options.C: The sorting facility automatically separates the paper for standard municipal recycling
options.D: The entire batch of waste must be treated as hazardous, increasing disposal costs

explanation: Cross-contamination forces the facility to process clean refuse through expensive hazardous treatment channels. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended capacity limit for waste bags and containers before they are sealed and removed?

options.A: Completely packed to the brim
options.B: Three-quarters full
options.C: One-quarter capacity
options.D: One-half capacity

explanation: Containers are sealed at three-quarters capacity to allow safe handling and prevent tearing or accidental spills during closure. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h5)

question: Why is strict limitation of temporary storage time crucial in tropical climates?

options.A: To comply with international tax exemptions for medical facilities
options.B: To prevent rapid decomposition, vector attraction, and unpleasant odor generation
options.C: To ensure that waste collection staff complete their shifts before dark
options.D: To allow waste bags to be reused multiple times across different wards

explanation: Warm temperatures accelerate organic breakdown and attract flies, rodents, and other disease vectors if waste lingers too long. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h5)

question: Which waste treatment method uses high-pressure steam sterilization to neutralize pathogens?

options.A: Open dumping
options.B: Autoclaving
options.C: Incineration
options.D: Chemical burial

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to destroy microorganisms, rendering infectious materials safe for standard disposal routes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h6)

question: Which of the following disposal methods is NOT suitable for untreated anatomical or infectious pathological waste?

options.A: Direct placement into unlined municipal open dumps
options.B: Encapsulation in solid containers prior to burial
options.C: Steam sterilization followed by secure shredding
options.D: High-temperature controlled medical waste incineration

explanation: Untreated infectious or pathological waste poses severe public health and environmental risks if dumped without prior hazard neutralization. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h6)

question: What is the most critical immediate action following an accidental needlestick injury with a used hollow-bore needle?

options.A: Applying a tight tourniquet above the injury site immediately
options.B: Continuing the shift and reporting the incident at the end of the week
options.C: Soaking the entire hand in a concentrated chlorine solution
options.D: Washing the site with soap and water and reporting for evaluation

explanation: Immediate washing reduces viral load, and prompt reporting ensures timely access to post-exposure prophylaxis. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: Why is mandatory hepatitis B vaccination emphasized for healthcare workers and waste handlers?

options.A: To eliminate the need for wearing gloves during clinical procedures
options.B: To protect workers from chemical burns caused by concentrated disinfectants
options.C: To prevent airborne transmission of tuberculosis during waste sorting
options.D: To provide active immunity against bloodborne transmission risks from sharps injuries

explanation: Hepatitis B is highly infectious through blood and needle exposure, making vaccination an essential occupational safeguard. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: What proportion of total waste generated in a healthcare setting is typically classified as hazardous?

options.A: 95 to 99 percent
options.B: 75 to 90 percent
options.C: 50 to 60 percent
options.D: 10 to 25 percent

explanation: The vast majority of hospital waste is general domestic refuse, leaving only a minority fraction classified as hazardous infectious or chemical waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h1)

question: Why is the improper management of health care waste particularly dangerous in clinical environments?

options.A: It reduces the overall bed occupancy rate of the hospital
options.B: It facilitates the spread of drug-resistant pathogens and needle injuries
options.C: It immediately causes structural damage to municipal sewage pipes
options.D: It directly increases the operational budget of the facility

explanation: Hazardous medical waste contains infectious agents and sharp objects that pose direct biological threats to staff, patients, and waste handlers if mismanaged. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h1)

question: Which color container is universally designated for the disposal of used needles and safety syringes?

options.A: Black municipal bin
options.B: Blue recycling bin
options.C: Transparent plastic bag
options.D: Yellow safety box

explanation: Puncture-resistant yellow safety boxes are specifically designed to collect sharps safely at the point of care. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary consequence of placing infectious waste into a general municipal waste bin?

options.A: The entire combined volume must now be treated as hazardous waste
options.B: The infectious waste becomes chemically inert within hours
options.C: The municipal waste collection fee is automatically waived
options.D: The recycling facility will automatically separate the materials

explanation: When hazardous waste contaminates general refuse, the whole batch loses its domestic classification and requires costly specialized disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which an autoclave sterilizes infectious medical waste?

options.A: Chemical bleaching
options.B: Open flame combustion
options.C: Pressurized saturated steam
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation

explanation: Autoclaves use high pressure and high-temperature steam to destroy microorganisms within medical waste effectively. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h3)

question: Which type of medical waste cannot be effectively processed using a standard steam autoclave?

options.A: Anatomical body parts and chemical drugs
options.B: Used disposable syringes
options.C: Contaminated laboratory cultures
options.D: Wound dressing gauze and bandages

explanation: Autoclaves are unsuited for chemical waste and large anatomical specimens, which generally require high-temperature incineration. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of encapsulation in health care waste management?

options.A: To sterilize surgical instruments before reuse
options.B: To generate electricity through microbial decomposition
options.C: To immobilize chemical and pharmaceutical waste in a solid matrix
options.D: To recycle plastic syringes into new equipment

explanation: Encapsulation binds hazardous chemical or pharmaceutical agents within cement or plastic to prevent environmental leaching. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: Which clinical waste stream is most commonly treated using liquid chemical disinfectants before disposal?

options.A: Laboratory cultures and infectious liquid waste
options.B: Plaster of Paris casting fragments
options.C: Cardboard packaging from intravenous fluids
options.D: Expired metal surgical blades

explanation: Liquid cultures and infectious fluids are readily mixed with chemical disinfectants to neutralize pathogens prior to drainage or disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h4)

question: At what capacity should a sharps safety box be sealed and replaced to prevent puncture injuries?

options.A: Half full
options.B: Three-quarters full
options.C: One-quarter full
options.D: Completely packed to the brim

explanation: Safety boxes must be closed when three-quarters full to leave sufficient margin and prevent accidental needle punctures from overfilling. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary function of a leachate collection system in a modern sanitary landfill?

options.A: To incinerate combustible gases produced by decomposing refuse
options.B: To prevent toxic liquid runoff from contaminating groundwater
options.C: To generate steam pressure for sterilizing incoming medical waste
options.D: To wash medical waste trucks before they leave the facility

explanation: Leachate systems capture contaminated liquids percolating through waste, protecting local water tables from dangerous chemical and biological seepage. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h5)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Immediately cauterize the puncture wound with a hot probe
options.B: Bandage the finger tightly without washing to trap the blood
options.C: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site

explanation: Immediate washing with soap and water helps flush out pathogens before seeking prompt medical evaluation and post-exposure prophylaxis. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable practice regarding sharps handling in a clinical setting?

options.A: Discarding needles without manual recapping
options.B: Using puncture-resistant safety boxes at the point of care
options.C: Reporting all needle-stick exposures immediately
options.D: Manually recapping used needles with both hands

explanation: Manual recapping using two hands is a leading cause of needle-stick injuries and is strictly prohibited in safety protocols. [learn more](GST114_U6_T13#GST114_U6_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a parasitic relationship?

options.A: The parasite lives at the expense of the host to obtain nutrients
options.B: The host actively consumes the parasite for metabolic energy
options.C: Both organisms derive mutual benefit from the association
options.D: Both organisms live independently without any physiological contact

explanation: Parasitism is defined by a non-mutual relationship where one organism benefits at the direct expense of another host. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why is parasitology of particular clinical importance in regions like Nigeria?

options.A: Favorable climatic conditions and sanitation gaps promote high transmission rates
options.B: Parasites in tropical climates have simpler single-host life cycles
options.C: Modern diagnostic laboratories are completely absent in urban centers
options.D: Local populations have total genetic immunity against all known protozoa

explanation: Environmental warmth, vector proliferation, and water infrastructure challenges create high endemicity for many parasitic diseases in sub-Saharan Africa. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h1)

question: Where do endoparasites reside relative to the human body?

options.A: On the outer skin surface and hair follicles
options.B: Within the clothing fibers worn by the host
options.C: Exclusively in stagnant water and soil beds
options.D: Inside internal tissues, blood, or the intestinal tract

explanation: Endoparasites live within the internal environment of the host body, whereas ectoparasites inhabit the exterior surface. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h2)

question: What distinguishes a definitive host from an intermediate host?

options.A: The definitive host harbors the sexually mature stage of the parasite
options.B: The definitive host provides no nutritional support to the parasite
options.C: The intermediate host is always a vertebrate animal species
options.D: The intermediate host transmits the pathogen only via aerosol droplets

explanation: Sexual reproduction of the parasite always occurs within the definitive host, while asexual multiplication or larval development takes place in the intermediate host. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which category of medical parasites consists of single-celled microscopic organisms?

options.A: Nematodes
options.B: Cestodes
options.C: Trematodes
options.D: Protozoa

explanation: Protozoa are unicellular eukaryotic microorganisms, whereas nematodes, cestodes, and trematodes are multicellular helminths. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h3)

question: A patient is diagnosed with an intestinal tapeworm infection. To which major classification group does this parasite belong?

options.A: Bacterial vectors
options.B: Helminths
options.C: Protozoa
options.D: Arthropods

explanation: Tapeworms are cestodes, which form a major subgroup of multicellular helminths. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h3)

question: How do hookworm larvae typically gain entry into the human body from soil?

options.A: Through inhalation of contaminated dry dust particles
options.B: By consuming unwashed fruits and vegetables
options.C: Via the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito
options.D: By active penetration through the intact skin

explanation: Hookworm infective filariform larvae in contaminated soil penetrate human skin, usually when individuals walk barefoot. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which transmission mechanism is characterized by an insect vector injecting the parasite during a blood meal?

options.A: Congenital transplacental spread
options.B: Fecal-oral ingestion
options.C: Direct skin penetration
options.D: Vector-borne inoculation

explanation: Vector-borne transmission occurs when blood-feeding arthropods introduce pathogens directly into the host circulatory system. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which white blood cell type is characteristically elevated during a tissue-invasive helminth infection?

options.A: Erythrocytes
options.B: Neutrophils
options.C: Eosinophils
options.D: Platelets

explanation: Eosinophilia is a hallmark hematological finding in response to multicellular helminthic parasite invasions. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is a primary mechanism by which parasites manage to establish chronic, long-term infections in humans?

options.A: Stimulating total permanent shutdown of the host bone marrow
options.B: Undergoing rapid antigenic variation to evade immune recognition
options.C: Exclusively inhabiting non-vascularized areas of the skeleton
options.D: Relying solely on host cell apoptosis for their own reproduction

explanation: Many parasites alter their surface antigens over time, preventing the host's immune system from effectively clearing the persistent infection. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h5)

question: What laboratory method is most commonly utilized in routine clinical settings to diagnose malaria?

options.A: Thick and thin blood film microscopy
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid culture
options.C: Urinalysis reagent strip screening
options.D: Stool occult blood chemical testing

explanation: Microscopic examination of stained thick and thin blood smears remains the primary diagnostic tool for identifying malaria parasites. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h6)

question: Why is a detailed travel and residential history essential when evaluating a patient with suspected parasitic disease?

options.A: Different parasites are endemic to specific geographic regions and climates
options.B: Parasites can only infect individuals who possess a specific foreign passport
options.C: Treatment medications are legally restricted based on international travel records
options.D: Laboratory equipment functions differently based on the patient's country of origin

explanation: Geographic exposure history helps clinicians narrow down potential parasitic agents that thrive in particular environmental conditions. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h6)

question: Which intervention represents a key community-level preventive measure against vector-borne parasitic infections like malaria?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics to all infants
options.B: Performing routine surgical appendectomies in endemic zones
options.C: Enforcing mandatory isolation wards for infected patients
options.D: Promoting the regular use of insecticide-treated bed nets

explanation: Insecticide-treated bed nets reduce human-vector contact, protecting individuals from bites by nocturnal disease-transmitting mosquitoes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is an important component of nursing care for a patient undergoing treatment for a severe intestinal parasite infection?

options.A: Encouraging strict complete bed rest without any physical movement
options.B: Applying topical antiseptic dressings over the abdominal wall daily
options.C: Monitoring hydration status and managing gastrointestinal symptoms
options.D: Restricting all oral fluid intake to starve the remaining parasites

explanation: Gastrointestinal parasites frequently cause diarrhea and malabsorption, making fluid balance assessment and supportive care vital nursing responsibilities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of environmental sanitation in public health?

options.A: Regulating international trade tariffs on pharmaceutical imports
options.B: Eliminating the need for clinical hospital infrastructure
options.C: Controlling physical environmental factors that negatively affect health
options.D: Maximizing industrial agricultural output in rural districts

explanation: Environmental sanitation focuses specifically on managing environmental elements like water, waste, and vectors that threaten human well-being. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why does rapid urbanization without infrastructural expansion increase public health risks?

options.A: It overwhelms municipal waste and water systems, causing environmental contamination
options.B: It immediately increases the genetic mutation rate of local pathogenic bacteria
options.C: It forces healthcare workers to migrate away from densely populated areas
options.D: It decreases the availability of commercial food products in local markets

explanation: When cities grow faster than their sanitation infrastructure, waste management fails, leading to pollution and disease spread. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which demographic group is most vulnerable to the severe impacts of parasitic infections in Nigeria?

options.A: Adolescent males working in corporate offices
options.B: Retired military personnel living in urban centers
options.C: High-income earners residing in gated communities
options.D: School-aged children and pregnant women

explanation: Children and pregnant women suffer disproportionately due to developing immune systems and high physiological demands, leading to severe complications like anemia. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h2)

question: How do tropical climates in regions like Nigeria influence parasitic infections?

options.A: They prevent parasites from entering human hosts through the skin
options.B: Warm temperatures and high humidity support the life cycles of protozoa and helminths
options.C: They shorten the lifespan of vectors to reduce disease transmission
options.D: They completely sterilize soil and water sources during the dry season

explanation: Many parasites and their intermediate vectors thrive in warm, moist environments, accelerating their maturation and transmission cycles. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h2)

question: How do hookworm larvae typically gain entry into the human body?

options.A: Bites from infected mosquitoes during the night
options.B: Active penetration through bare skin in contaminated soil
options.C: Inhalation of airborne spores in crowded rooms
options.D: Ingestion of unwashed fruits and vegetables

explanation: Hookworm infection occurs when infectious larvae in damp soil burrow through the skin of individuals walking barefoot. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h3)

question: A patient presents with an infection acquired while swimming in a slow-moving freshwater stream. Which parasite is the most likely culprit?

options.A: Plasmodium falciparum
options.B: Entamoeba histolytica
options.C: Ascaris lumbricoides
options.D: Schistosoma species

explanation: Schistosomiasis is contracted when skin comes into contact with freshwater containing free-swimming larval forms released by infected snails. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism driving the transmission of many intestinal parasites?

options.A: Transplacental transfer
options.B: The faecal-oral route
options.C: Direct droplet inhalation
options.D: Blood transfusion accidents

explanation: Intestinal parasites largely spread when microscopic eggs or cysts from feces find their way into the mouth via contaminated hands, food, or water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h4)

question: Which factor best explains why treating a patient with antiparasitic medication without improving sanitation often leads to reinfection?

options.A: Medications lose potency when manufactured in tropical climates
options.B: The patient continues to live in an environment where pathogens remain in the water and soil
options.C: Immune systems reject the chemical composition of standard anthelminthics
options.D: Parasites develop permanent immunity to pharmaceutical agents within days

explanation: Pharmacotherapy cures the current infection, but without environmental sanitation changes, ongoing exposure to contaminated surroundings causes rapid reinfection. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h4)

question: Which physical finding is commonly observed during the assessment of a child with a heavy hookworm burden?

options.A: Pallor due to chronic anemia
options.B: Rigid paralysis of the lower limbs
options.C: Jaundice from acute liver failure
options.D: Hypertension and peripheral edema

explanation: Hookworms feed on intestinal blood, leading to chronic blood loss and subsequent iron-deficiency anemia, which manifests as pale mucous membranes and skin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h5)

question: Why do many individuals harboring intestinal parasites remain asymptomatic?

options.A: Asymptomatic carriers possess a genetic immunity to reinfection
options.B: Human immune systems instantly destroy all invading helminths
options.C: Parasites secrete local anesthetics that block nerve impulses in the gut
options.D: Low parasite burdens often cause minimal disruption to host physiology

explanation: A small number of parasites may not overwhelm the host's nutritional reserves or cause significant tissue damage, resulting in silent carriage. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which medication class is commonly prescribed as a first-line treatment for soil-transmitted helminths?

options.A: Bronchodilators
options.B: Antihypertensives
options.C: Anticonvulsants
options.D: Anthelminthics

explanation: Anthelminthic drugs like albendazole and mebendazole are specifically designed to eradicate parasitic worms from the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h6)

question: A nurse is caring for a severely malnourished child admitted with a heavy roundworm infection. What should be an immediate priority alongside administering the prescribed anthelminthic drug?

options.A: Restricting all fluid intake to rest the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Administering broad-spectrum intravenous chemotherapy
options.C: Placing the child in strict airborne isolation
options.D: Initiating nutritional support and monitoring hydration status

explanation: Parasitic infections deplete host nutrients and cause fluid imbalances; nutritional rehabilitation and hydration management are critical alongside deworming. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why are mass drug administration programs often implemented in endemic communities?

options.A: To replace the need for clean water infrastructure in rural towns
options.B: To test the commercial viability of new pharmaceutical compounds
options.C: To rapidly reduce the overall parasite burden and morbidity across the population
options.D: To permanently immunize individuals against future parasite exposure

explanation: Treating entire at-risk populations simultaneously lowers transmission dynamics and prevents severe disease manifestations, especially in children. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended public health measure for preventing hookworm infection?

options.A: Encouraging the regular consumption of raw, unwashed vegetables
options.B: Implementing community-wide mass deworming campaigns
options.C: Promoting the consistent use of protective footwear outdoors
options.D: Constructing sanitary latrines to eliminate open defecation

explanation: Eating unwashed produce exposes individuals to pathogens and does not prevent hookworm, which is contracted through skin contact with contaminated soil. [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary public health objective of safe sewage management?

options.A: To completely eliminate industrial chemical production
options.B: To generate organic fertilizer for agricultural lands
options.C: To break the epidemiological chain of the fecal-oral route
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of municipal water treatment

explanation: Proper waste management stops pathogens in human excreta from re-entering the human body through water or food supplies. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h1)

question: How does improper sewage disposal directly threaten local water sources during the rainy season?

options.A: By increasing the mineral hardness of deep borehole water
options.B: By accelerating the evaporation rate of nearby surface reservoirs
options.C: By causing chemical reactions that deplete dissolved oxygen
options.D: By allowing surface runoff to leach waste into high water tables

explanation: Heavy rainfall floods poorly contained waste sites, carrying pathogens directly into shallow wells and groundwater tables used for drinking. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h1)

question: What percentage of raw sewage mass is composed of pure water?

options.A: Exactly 50.0%
options.B: Approximately 99.9%
options.C: No more than 10.2%
options.D: Roughly 75.5%

explanation: The vast majority of sewage is simply liquid carrier water, with only a fraction of a percent containing actual solid waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the ecological function of saprophytic bacteria found within raw sewage?

options.A: They accelerate the chemical evaporation of the liquid component.
options.B: They directly target and destroy all pathogenic viruses present.
options.C: They break down complex organic matter suspended in the waste.
options.D: They synthesize complex heavy metals into harmless mineral salts.

explanation: Saprophytes feed on dead and decaying organic material, driving the natural decomposition process within wastewater. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which pathogenic agent is primarily responsible for causing epidemic cholera through contaminated water?

options.A: Entamoeba histolytica
options.B: Hepatitis A virus
options.C: Vibrio cholerae
options.D: Ascaris lumbricoides

explanation: Vibrio cholerae is the bacterium that causes cholera, characterized by severe watery diarrhea and rapid dehydration. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why are protozoan parasites like Giardia particularly difficult to eliminate from contaminated water sources?

options.A: They multiply rapidly in the absence of any organic nutrients.
options.B: They produce airborne spores that bypass water filtration beds.
options.C: They actively consume chlorine gas added during purification.
options.D: Their hard cyst stage resists standard environmental conditions.

explanation: Cysts form a protective outer shell that shields the parasite from harsh weather, drying, and normal disinfectant levels. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary function of the heavy solid matter that settles at the bottom of a septic tank?

options.A: It forms sludge that undergoes anaerobic digestion.
options.B: It hardens into a permanent structural concrete floor.
options.C: It pumps itself into the municipal water distribution grid.
options.D: It dissolves completely into pure drinking water overnight.

explanation: Settled solids accumulate as sludge at the base of the tank, where anaerobic bacteria break down a portion of the organic mass over time. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why must on-site soakaway pits and septic tanks undergo periodic emptying?

options.A: To allow structural engineers to inspect the exterior concrete for hairline cracks
options.B: To replenish the supply of active aerobic bacteria needed for liquid treatment
options.C: To extract concentrated chemical fertilizers for local agricultural use
options.D: To prevent the accumulation of sludge and scum from clogging the drain field

explanation: If solids are allowed to fill the tank, they spill over into the absorption field, sealing the soil pores and causing wastewater to back up. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h4)

question: What physical force typically moves wastewater through underground gravity pipes in a municipal network?

options.A: High-pressure steam
options.B: Magnetic levitation
options.C: Geothermal boiling
options.D: Gravitational pull

explanation: Gravity sewers are engineered with a consistent downward slope to allow wastewater to flow naturally without constant mechanical pumping. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary danger when an underground municipal sewage pipe ruptures directly adjacent to a corroded water supply pipe?

options.A: Complete chemical neutralization of all chlorine in the drinking water
options.B: Massive electrical shorts within the municipal power transformers
options.C: Cross-contamination leading to waterborne disease outbreaks
options.D: A sudden drop in water pressure throughout the entire city grid

explanation: Leaking sewage can seep into compromised drinking water lines, directly introducing pathogens into household taps. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which stage of wastewater treatment primarily relies on physical screening and sedimentation to remove heavy suspended solids?

options.A: Quaternary treatment
options.B: Tertiary treatment
options.C: Secondary treatment
options.D: Primary treatment

explanation: Primary treatment is the initial mechanical phase that catches grit and allows heavier particles to settle out of the liquid. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h6)

question: What is the main biological mechanism utilized during secondary wastewater treatment?

options.A: Ultraviolet radiation mutating the DNA of floating bacteria
options.B: Aerobic microorganisms consuming dissolved organic pollutants
options.C: Anaerobic evaporation stripping heavy metals into the atmosphere
options.D: Chemical coagulation binding mineral salts into solid flakes

explanation: Secondary treatment introduces air into wastewater tanks to support aerobic bacteria that feed on and break down remaining organic waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h6)

question: What does a high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) level indicate about a polluted water body?

options.A: High levels of organic waste consuming available dissolved oxygen
options.B: Optimal conditions for commercial fish breeding and aquaculture
options.C: Total absence of any microbial life within the water column
options.D: Excessive concentrations of pure oxygen produced by aquatic plants

explanation: High BOD means microorganisms are working overtime to digest abundant organic pollution, rapidly depleting oxygen required by fish. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h7)

question: Why is the bioaccumulation of toxins in aquatic food chains a significant concern for human health?

options.A: Fish exposed to raw sewage lose their nutritional caloric value entirely.
options.B: Top-predator fish concentrate heavy metals to levels harmful to consumers.
options.C: Aquatic plants absorb sewage nutrients and release toxic gas into the air.
options.D: Contaminated water causes immediate structural collapse of fishing boats.

explanation: Toxins multiply in concentration as they move up the food chain, meaning humans eating large fish ingest dangerous cumulative doses. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h7)

question: Which nursing activity represents a primary preventive measure against waterborne diseases in a community?

options.A: Performing routine diagnostic blood transfusions in hospital wards
options.B: Administering intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics to surgical patients
options.C: Suturing traumatic lacerations sustained during industrial accidents
options.D: Conducting education on hand hygiene and safe water storage

explanation: Teaching healthy sanitation habits stops diseases before they start by interrupting transmission paths at the household level. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h8)

question: What is an essential collaborative responsibility of community health nurses during a sudden cholera outbreak?

options.A: Demanding the immediate closure of all local food processing plants
options.B: Designing blueprints for municipal underground sewer pipe networks
options.C: Working with environmental officers to trace water contamination sources
options.D: Personally incinerating all solid domestic waste within the city limits

explanation: Controlling an epidemic requires teamwork between clinicians treating patients and public health staff finding and fixing the root environmental source. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h8)

question: What is the primary infection control purpose of proper hospital waste management?

options.A: Interrupting pathogen transmission chains
options.B: Complying with architectural guidelines
options.C: Reducing hospital utility costs
options.D: Improving hospital public relations

explanation: Proper waste disposal physically removes contaminated materials from the environment, stopping microorganisms from spreading to new hosts. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why do improperly managed healthcare waste sites present severe microbiological risks?

options.A: Discarded items neutralize all hospital disinfectants
options.B: Municipal waste eliminates local microbial populations
options.C: Trash bags automatically attract airborne spores
options.D: Organic waste creates breeding environments for pathogens

explanation: Discarded organic materials combined with moisture allow bacteria and other microorganisms to multiply rapidly if not contained. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which category does a used surgical scalpel blade belong to?

options.A: Sharps waste
options.B: Pathological waste
options.C: Pharmaceutical waste
options.D: General domestic waste

explanation: Any device with a point or edge that can puncture skin, such as a scalpel or needle, is classified strictly as sharps waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h2)

question: A patient's amputated limb removed during surgery is best categorized as what type of waste?

options.A: Pathological waste
options.B: Chemical waste
options.C: General waste
options.D: Pharmaceutical waste

explanation: Pathological waste includes human tissues, organs, and body parts generated during surgeries and autopsies. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which bloodborne pathogen is most commonly transmitted via a contaminated needle stick injury?

options.A: Hepatitis B virus
options.B: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.C: Influenza virus
options.D: Salmonella typhi

explanation: Hepatitis B has a high infectivity rate through percutaneous exposure to contaminated blood and sharps. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h3)

question: How do vectors like flies and mosquitoes contribute to the danger of improperly managed medical waste?

options.A: They neutralize toxic chemicals present in pharmaceutical refuse
options.B: They accelerate the biodegradation of heavy plastics
options.C: They transport pathogens from exposed waste back into the community
options.D: They consume infectious sharps safely

explanation: Flies and mosquitoes feed on contaminated organic matter and act as mechanical vectors, transferring disease-causing microorganisms to populated spaces. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h3)

question: Where should the segregation of healthcare waste take place?

options.A: Inside the central laundry room
options.B: Outside the hospital gate
options.C: At the final incineration site
options.D: At the point of generation

explanation: Waste must be sorted immediately as it is produced to prevent cross-contamination and ensure proper categorization. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary consequence of placing infectious waste into a bin designated for general domestic refuse?

options.A: The municipal waste facility will automatically sterilize it
options.B: The entire waste batch becomes hazardous and increases safety risks
options.C: The volume of hazardous waste decreases overall
options.D: The color coding of the facility changes permanently

explanation: Mixing infectious materials into general waste contaminates the whole load, endangering sanitation workers and community dump sites. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended capacity to which a waste bag should be filled before tying?

options.A: Exclusively half full
options.B: Completely packed to the brim
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: One-quarter full

explanation: Bags should be tied off at three-quarters capacity to allow safe handling and prevent tearing or spills. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: When transporting waste bags through hospital corridors, why should staff hold them away from their bodies?

options.A: To prevent injury if an improperly discarded sharp protrudes through the bag
options.B: To ensure the weight is distributed evenly across the shoulders
options.C: To allow faster walking speeds during shift changes
options.D: To comply with aesthetic hospital uniform policies

explanation: Holding waste bags away from the body protects the torso and legs from accidental punctures caused by rogue needles or glass. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which waste treatment method uses high-temperature dry oxidation to reduce waste to ash?

options.A: Microwaving
options.B: Sanitary landfilling
options.C: Autoclaving
options.D: Incineration

explanation: Incineration burns waste at very high temperatures, destroying pathogens and reducing volume into inert ash. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: Which clinical material is most appropriate for processing via an autoclave?

options.A: Large anatomical body parts
options.B: Expired heavy chemical solvents
options.C: General laboratory cultures and infectious plastics
options.D: Radioactive diagnostic elements

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to effectively sterilize infectious laboratory waste and clinical instruments before disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the immediate first action a nurse should take following an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Apply an alcoholic disinfectant without washing

options.C: Wash the site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Squeeze the puncture wound tightly to stop circulation

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective engineering control for preventing sharps injuries among nursing staff?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands before disposal

options.C: Using needleless intravenous connection systems
options.D: Utilizing retractable syringe mechanisms

question: Which Nigerian federal agency is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards and regulations, including medical waste?

question: A Nigerian clinic experiences a shortage of certified yellow biohazard bags. What is the most appropriate interim nursing action?

options.A: Utilize sturdy alternative containers that prevent leaks and punctures while maintaining clear hazard identification

options.C: Dump infectious waste into the general municipal bin until supplies arrive
options.D: Stop all clinical procedures that generate waste

question: What primary change defines water pollution?

options.B: Introduction of toxic foreign substances that degrade quality
options.C: Excessive mineralization from deep underground rock layers
options.D: Natural evaporation of mineral content from aquifers

explanation: Water pollution is specifically characterized by the presence of harmful contaminants introduced by human or industrial activities that ruin its usability. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why is water pollution a critical concern in resource-limited healthcare environments?

options.A: Chemical manufacturing plants strictly regulate their own river discharges
options.B: Communities often depend directly on vulnerable surface water sources
options.C: Rainfall completely neutralizes industrial waste compounds instantly
options.D: Municipal tap water systems filter out all biological pathogens automatically

explanation: When piped infrastructure is lacking, populations must draw from rivers and streams that frequently harbor untreated pollutants. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h1)

question: Which category of water pollutant includes nitrates and phosphates from agricultural fertilizers?

options.A: Nutrient pollutants
options.B: Heavy metal pollutants
options.C: Biological pollutants
options.D: Radioactive pollutants

question: What is the primary danger associated with chemical pollutants such as lead and mercury in water supplies?

options.A: They accumulate in body tissues and cause chronic organ toxicity
options.B: They increase water clarity while stripping away natural minerals
options.C: They immediately freeze water sources during warm weather seasons
options.D: They deplete oxygen levels by promoting rapid bacterial multiplication

explanation: Heavy metals do not easily break down and tend to bioaccumulate in living organisms, leading to severe neurological and renal damage over time. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h2)

question: What distinguishes a point source of water pollution from a non-point source?

options.A: It discharges pollutants through a clearly identifiable, localized outlet
options.B: It changes location constantly based on seasonal rainfall patterns
options.C: It only releases biological pathogens instead of chemical waste
options.D: It originates exclusively from heavy agricultural fertilizer runoff

explanation: Point sources have a single, measurable point of origin like an industrial discharge pipe. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h3)

question: A patient living near an unregulated agricultural farm is exposed to runoff water. Which pollution source category does this represent?

options.A: Non-point source
options.B: Point source
options.C: Pointless source
options.D: Thermal source

explanation: Agricultural runoff spreads across large expanses of land before entering water bodies, making it a classic non-point contamination source. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which bacterium is famously responsible for causing epidemic waterborne cholera?

options.A: Vibrio cholerae
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation: Vibrio cholerae is the specific bacterial pathogen that produces enterotoxins causing severe, rapid fluid loss through watery diarrhea. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary pathophysiological threat facing a patient with a severe waterborne gastrointestinal infection?

options.A: Sudden accumulation of heavy metals in the renal cortex
options.B: Complete destruction of red blood cell production capacity
options.C: Rapid and life-threatening fluid and electrolyte depletion
options.D: Permanent hardening of major arterial blood vessel walls

explanation: Intestinal pathogens cause intense secretory diarrhea and vomiting, quickly leading to hypovolemic shock if fluids are not aggressively replaced. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h4)

question: What term describes the process where excess nutrients cause explosive algal growth and oxygen depletion in water bodies?

options.A: Chlorination
options.B: Biomagnification
options.C: Salinization
options.D: Eutrophication

explanation: Eutrophication occurs when nutrient enrichment overstimulates algae, leading to oxygen-depleting decay that harms aquatic life. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h5)

question: How does biomagnification affect organisms located at the very top of an aquatic food chain?

options.A: They experience sudden immunity to all forms of bacterial infection
options.B: They multiply rapidly due to increased availability of dissolved nutrients
options.C: They accumulate dangerously high concentrations of persistent toxins
options.D: They adapt by converting chemical pollutants into harmless plant tissue

explanation: As predators consume multiple contaminated prey items, fat-soluble toxins multiply in concentration at each trophic level. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h5)

question: Which organism is commonly used as a primary biological indicator for fecal contamination in water testing?

options.A: Bacillus anthracis
options.B: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.C: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: E. coli resides in the intestines of warm-blooded animals, making its presence in water a reliable marker of fecal pollution. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why is turbidity testing an important routine parameter for water quality assessment?

options.A: High turbidity automatically confirms the presence of dissolved mercury
options.B: Cloudy water can shield harmful pathogens from disinfection processes
options.C: It measures the exact concentration of nitrates from fertilizers
options.D: Clear water guarantees total absence of chemical toxins and metals

explanation: Suspended particles cause turbidity and can physically shelter microorganisms from ultraviolet light or chlorine disinfection. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of secondary wastewater treatment?

options.B: Adding heavy doses of fluoride to strengthen community teeth
options.C: Physical screening and settling of large floating trash objects

question: Which method is typically employed during tertiary treatment to destroy remaining microscopic pathogens?

options.A: Coarse screening through wire mesh metal grates
options.B: Gravity sedimentation in large outdoor holding ponds
options.C: Ultraviolet light irradiation or chemical disinfection
options.D: Evaporation of water through direct sunlight exposure

question: What is an effective point-of-use water purification method community nurses can teach households?

options.A: Boiling water vigorously before drinking

options.D: Leaving untreated water in open plastic buckets

question: Which activity best illustrates a proactive public health nursing intervention regarding water safety?

options.A: Educating villagers on safe domestic water storage and hygiene
options.B: Constructing municipal industrial sewage treatment plants alone

options.D: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every household member

question: What primary environmental stressor do airborne microorganisms face while suspended in the atmosphere?

options.A: Excessive moisture and humidity
options.B: Constant magnetic field interference

question: Why is the intersection of atmospheric pollution and microbiology clinically relevant in urban centers?

options.A: Urban heat islands cause all airborne bacteria to undergo immediate cell lysis
options.B: Pollutants chemically sterilize the air column, completely eliminating all biological agents
options.C: Chemical smog prevents microorganisms from reproducing within human host tissues

question: The incomplete combustion of carbon-based fuels, especially from faulty indoor generators, primarily releases which toxic gas?

options.A: Nitrogen gas
options.B: Ground-level ozone
options.C: Sulphur dioxide
options.D: Carbon monoxide

explanation: Faulty or poorly ventilated combustion engines produce carbon monoxide, a gas that binds tightly to hemoglobin and starves tissues of oxygen. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h2)

question: How is ground-level ozone fundamentally different from primary pollutants like sulphur dioxide?

options.A: It only exists in the stratosphere and has no impact on human respiration
options.B: It is emitted directly from factory smokestacks during night shifts
options.C: It is formed through atmospheric chemical reactions driven by sunlight interacting with precursor gases

question: What term describes suspended atmospheric particles that are explicitly of biological origin?

options.A: Hydrocarbons
options.B: Particulate metals

explanation: Bioaerosols encompass any microscopic living or dead biological matter, including spores, viruses, and bacteria, suspended in a gas medium. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h3)

question: Why do fungal spores and bacterial endospores remain viable in the atmosphere for extended periods?

options.A: They consume surrounding chemical pollutants for continuous cellular replication

options.C: They actively generate their own propulsive energy using solar panels
options.D: Their durable outer coats protect them against desiccation and environmental stressors

question: What atmospheric phenomenon traps a layer of dense, cool air and pollutants beneath a warm air layer near the ground?

options.A: Thermal inversion
options.B: Stratospheric depletion
options.C: Tropospheric condensation
options.D: Barometric divergence

question: How does heavy rainfall immediately affect airborne biological particles?

options.C: It forces all surface microbes to launch into the stratosphere

question: Which respiratory structures are deep enough to be penetrated by fine particulate matter (PM2.5) that bypasses nasal filtration?

options.B: Nasal turbinates and sinuses
options.C: The epiglottis and vocal cords

question: A patient with chronic asthma presents with acute respiratory distress after spending hours outdoors during a heavy smog advisory. What primary pathophysiological process most likely occurred in their airways?

question: What clinical diagnostic tool is primarily used to measure airflow obstruction and lung volumes in patients with respiratory symptoms?

question: Why is ambient air quality monitoring combined with clinical patient assessments by health agencies?

question: What is the primary rationale for placing a patient experiencing acute respiratory distress in a high-Fowler's position?

question: Which community-level intervention directly reduces indoor air pollution risks associated with traditional cooking methods?

question: What is NOT a primary responsibility of public health and nursing professionals in pollution prevention?

question: Why does improper healthcare waste management disproportionately impact community public health in developing regions?

question: Which category of medical waste includes expired medications and discarded chemical reagents?

question: How do poorly managed outdoor waste storage areas contribute to community disease transmission?

question: What is the maximum recommended fullness level for sealing a clinical waste bag before removal?

question: Which medical waste treatment method utilizes high-pressure steam for sterilization?

question: What is a major environmental concern associated with poorly operated medical waste incinerators?

question: Where can successfully autoclaved and treated medical waste be safely deposited?

question: What is the immediate action a nurse should take after sustaining a puncture injury from a used hypodermic needle?

question: What approximate percentage of total health care waste is typically classified as hazardous?

question: How do biological pathogens from improperly managed medical waste typically enter the human body of a waste handler?

options.D: Through airborne transmission across long geographical distances

question: What is the primary health hazard associated with genotoxic health care waste such as cytotoxic drugs?

question: A staff member drops an old mercury-containing blood pressure apparatus, causing the bulb to shatter. Which type of hazard does this spill present?

options.C: Enhancement of municipal recycling rates for single-use plastics

explanation: Uncontrolled disposal allows toxic leachate to seep into surrounding water tables and soil, threatening public health. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h5)

question: At what fill level should a puncture-resistant sharps container be securely sealed and removed?

options.A: Three-quarters full
options.B: Completely packed to the brim
options.C: One-quarter full
options.D: Only when it starts overflowing

explanation: Sharps boxes must never be overfilled; sealing them at three-quarters capacity prevents protruding needles and accidental punctures. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a standardized color-coded bin system in a clinical ward?

options.A: To ensure immediate and accurate segregation of waste at the point of generation
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing heavy-duty plastic garbage bags
options.C: To make the hospital environment appear more organized and aesthetically pleasing
options.D: To simplify the process of mixing all waste streams before final incineration

explanation: Color coding guides staff to separate hazardous materials from general refuse right where the waste is created. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency is prominently involved in enforcing environmental standards, including those related to hazardous waste?

options.A: NAPTIP
options.B: FRSC
options.C: NESREA
options.D: NCC

explanation: The National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency plays a central role in regulating environmental compliance in Nigeria. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of a professional nurse regarding health care waste management?

options.A: Reporting damaged or overfilled sharps containers to management
options.B: Complying with institutional protocols and national disposal guidelines
options.C: Supervising auxiliary staff to ensure proper segregation at the bedside
options.D: Transporting bulk hazardous waste to municipal landfills outside the facility

explanation: Nurses manage waste at the point of generation and ensure safe containment, but mass transport and final disposal are handled by specialized waste management teams. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h7)
